evidence_gaps: Notes is unavailable. The 17 actual Apple Reminders references support comparison of native spacing, typography, list edges and sheet chrome; they do not provide exact semantic counterparts for authentication, Live Activity, capacity, medium-detent or combined-settings states.

No physical haptic observation, spoken VoiceOver session, truly locked-phone capture, arbitrary wallpaper testing, native AX1–AX5 device states, live authentication/account/AutoFill completion or hardware frame-pacing evidence.
Enabled sign-in composition fixtures use inert local actions. They establish enabled paint and layout, not successful authentication.
Protected XCTest secure-keyboard stills are partial. Separate actual keyboard movie frames show first focus/refocus and are reviewed independently; partial stills are not full keyboard evidence.
Motion review consists of 48 actual sampled frames, three for each of 16 movies. There was no continuous playback assessment; no frame-pacing or dropped-frame claim follows.
Five-sample simulator launch/scroll measurements reflect host/XCTest conditions. They do not prove a hardware responsiveness improvement.

New filled loading-stability fixtures have no exact Round 7 filled/pending counterpart; new empty-password focus/refocus methods have no identical Round 7 method. The 60 paired states are scoped to their named deterministic fixtures.
Twelve unit renders are separate from the 332 canonical native screenshots. Source inspection of Activity layout tests does not establish native accessibility-size geometry.
Source and evidence hashes were independently checked, but supplied builds and test runs were not rerun by this reviewer.

categories.name: Visual hierarchy
categories.rationale: The board and Account hierarchy are coherent; sign-in still stacks too many similarly weighted horizontal elements.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Login composition originals show a bright native Apple slab competing with the credential CTA, especially in dark empty and password states. Reminders references keep one dominant task region.
categories.source_assessment: SignInView makes email contiguous and secondary providers explicit, but 24pt outer spacing, a Divider, 20pt form groups and a centered mode switch still accumulate visual bands.

categories.name: Spacing/grid
categories.rationale: Most margins and rows are consistent; the authentication composition needs a more deliberate grouping rhythm.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Board rows align on a stable text column; Account grouped insets look native. Default login has a large provider break while XXXL password content fills nearly the whole viewport.
categories.source_assessment: Explicit 20pt sign-in margins and nested 8/12/20/24pt gaps are predictable, but the mode-switch hit area and separator add height beyond the useful credential cluster.

categories.name: Typography scale
categories.rationale: System type is legible and restrained, with clear headers and body text.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Default and XXXL text preserve readable line breaks. Account Home Screen and Lock Screen prefixes now aid scanning; provider labels remain comparatively forceful.
categories.source_assessment: Semantic title2/headline/body/footnote styles and scaled metrics support consistent sizing; the Apple SDK asset retains its native typography.

categories.name: Dynamic Type
categories.rationale: XXXL is usable across the captured surfaces; larger accessibility sizes lack native evidence.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Long rows and expanded instructions wrap without observed horizontal clipping. Password heading remains above the secure field on first focus and refocus.
categories.source_assessment: Scaled metrics, vertical text growth, native list self-sizing and measured focus settlement support the evidence. AX1–AX5 unit renders do not establish device layout.

categories.name: Light contrast
categories.rationale: Primary information reads clearly in light mode.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Enabled login labels, board ink, errors and Account guidance remain distinct. Disabled fixture controls are identified as disabled rather than mistaken for production contrast failures.
categories.source_assessment: System semantic colors and primary-opacity helper text are appropriate. Recorded instruction samples exceed 7:1; enabled primary action checks exceed 4.5:1.

categories.name: Dark contrast
categories.rationale: Dark content is readable, though authentication contrast distribution is visually unbalanced.
categories.screenshot_assessment: White board text and Account instructions are clear. The white native Apple button draws more attention than the empty credential action, even though its label is crisp.
categories.source_assessment: Semantic foregrounds are sound; whiteOutline is intentionally fixed for the Apple asset. Disabled preview paint is separated from enabled inert composition fixtures.

categories.name: Iconography
categories.rationale: Icons are familiar, quiet and meaningful.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Completion circles, Account glyphs, keyboard dismissal and disclosure arrows have recognizable meanings. Red appears on the destructive trash icon, not as decoration.
categories.source_assessment: SF Symbols and the native SignInWithAppleButton are retained. Decorative glyphs are generally hidden from accessibility while controls have explicit labels.

categories.name: Safe area / Dynamic Island
categories.rationale: Captured app controls and expanded Activity content respect system regions.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Top controls sit below status/Island space; expanded Activity text and overflow footer clear the curved lower edge in representative originals.
categories.source_assessment: Native navigation and safeAreaInset handle app chrome. Empty compact Island regions avoid widened status overlap; expanded content has its own height budget and bottom margin.

categories.name: Scroll/pull-down / last row
categories.rationale: Last-row reachability is strong; the top edge still looks custom and imperfect.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Scrolled long/XXXL final rows retain their final ink above capacity guidance. Some partial-scroll states retain faint departing text immediately under the title area.
categories.source_assessment: UIKit refresh/reorder integration and hidden bottom edge preserve the last row. A custom 24pt gradient mask explains the remaining top fragments; the test checks only the narrow initial band.

categories.name: List rows
categories.rationale: Rows provide a calm, readable task surface.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Text aligns with completion circles on the first line; long rows expand and separators remain subtle. Persistent six-dot grips reduce text width and add some repeated furniture.
categories.source_assessment: A plain UICollectionView list with UIHostingConfiguration gives native self-sizing, separate 44pt completion/grip regions and explicit accessible reorder actions.

categories.name: Empty states
categories.rationale: The empty state explains what happens next without decorative framing.
categories.screenshot_assessment: All Clear reads clearly and the one-time setup guidance is useful. Compared with the sparse Reminders empty reference, the guidance adds density but remains coherent.
categories.source_assessment: ContentUnavailableView and a dismissible, persisted tip are appropriate. Guidance hides during focused composition and on loading/error/populated states.

categories.name: Composer ergonomics
categories.rationale: The bottom composer is clear and stays close to the keyboard.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Empty and nonempty XXXL composer originals retain draft text, a distinct add button and an unobstructed keyboard-dismiss action.
categories.source_assessment: A bottom safe-area inset, 1–4 line field, scaled visual button and minimum 44pt target are sensible. Capacity replaces the input instead of leaving a focusable dead field.

categories.name: Keyboard handling
categories.rationale: Primary focus geometry works; peripheral provider clipping weakens the settled composition.
categories.screenshot_assessment: First-focus/refocus movie frames retain Password and helper context above the keyboard. At XXXL, the Done strip can cut through the Apple button and leave a partial provider shape.
categories.source_assessment: Focus-frame preferences and scroll-idle restoration address heading settlement. The focused group alone is bounded; provider controls are not included in the settlement rule.

categories.name: Sheet presentation/detents
categories.rationale: Account sheets feel native and remain navigable at both detents.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Medium and large examples retain title, Done and scroll reachability. Native grouped surfaces resemble the Reminders sheet references without nested custom cards.
categories.source_assessment: Native medium/large presentation detents, visible drag indicator and scroll content interaction are suitable. Destructive work blocks dismissal while busy.

categories.name: Navigation clarity
categories.rationale: Core destinations and actions are understandable.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Your Board, Account and Sign In are unambiguous. The login mode-switch and provider choices are all visible but compete for attention.
categories.source_assessment: NavigationStack and native toolbar placement are clear. Explicit Account hints and password/link mode labels preserve meaning; no live external navigation was observed.

categories.name: Touch targets
categories.rationale: Source and supplied geometry support generous key controls.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Completion, reorder, add, Account and Done targets appear comfortably separated in representative captures.
categories.source_assessment: The source uses explicit 44pt or 48pt regions; current UI checks verify native frames for priority controls. No claim is made for uncaptured physical touch accuracy or every link width.

categories.name: Haptics
categories.rationale: The implementation uses sensible semantic feedback; tactile quality is unobserved.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Screenshots and movies provide no tactile evidence.
categories.source_assessment: Success/error sensory feedback and a selection generator on drag start are appropriate choices. Physical strength, timing and interaction with device settings still require hardware observation.

categories.name: Animation/transitions
categories.rationale: Sampled transitions preserve context, but the evidence cannot establish continuous motion quality.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Three actual samples per movie show expanded Island, dismissal, keyboard/refocus and app-close states. Some samples fall mid-system transition; they are not app defects by themselves.
categories.source_assessment: Short board animations respect Reduce Motion and UIKit handles reorder movement. reloadData and focus-driven scrollTo deserve real continuous observation; the recorded XCTest notification waits have no diagnosed UI cause.

categories.name: Loading states
categories.rationale: Loading communicates progress without moving following authentication controls.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Native spinner ink is visible in pending fixtures and the following mode switch/providers remain aligned with resting states.
categories.source_assessment: The title remains in layout with opacity zero and a regular ProgressView overlay; accessible labels retain the action plus in-progress meaning. Busy guards prevent duplicate submission.

categories.name: Error states
categories.rationale: Messages are readable and recovery is available; credential-error placement is detached.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Board and Account errors wrap cleanly with accessible contrast. Sign-in failure text sits after both providers, far from the credential action that caused it.
categories.source_assessment: Announcement policies deduplicate errors and reset on recovery. The sign-in error placement follows providerSection; moving it into the active credential cluster would improve association while preserving every word. Raw network-error wording is explicitly retained.

categories.name: VoiceOver/labels
categories.rationale: Source semantics are deliberate; spoken experience remains unverified.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Visible labels correspond to the intended actions, but images cannot establish traversal order or spoken clarity.
categories.source_assessment: Completion labels include reminder text, grip actions expose position/moves, duplicate row text is hidden, fields are named and announcement policies avoid repeats. The persistent visual Password heading is accessibilityHidden to prevent duplication.

categories.name: iOS HIG consistency
categories.rationale: The product mostly uses native surfaces with limited custom polish debt.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Native lists, sheets, semantic glyphs and system typography fit the platform. Login still reads like a custom vertical form and the board top fade is less convincing than native reference chrome.
categories.source_assessment: The architecture uses native components where useful. Custom gradient masking, mixed authentication button shapes and the separate Done inset are the main departures requiring visual judgment.

categories.name: Lock Screen / Live Activity
categories.rationale: The captured Activity surfaces are compact, legible and honest about overflow.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Short lines and +N more footers fit the Lock Screen-like banner and expanded Island in light/dark default/XXXL. Long lines truncate by design rather than overflowing.
categories.source_assessment: Separate line/height budgets and forced dark expanded-Island text are sound. Native background material is preserved. True lock, arbitrary wallpapers, privacy states and accessibility-size device behavior are unobserved.

categories.name: Sign-in/onboarding
categories.rationale: The email-first flow is clearer, but the full composition still falls short of calm native polish.
categories.screenshot_assessment: All 60 named comparisons show the changed order/grouping; default empty/filled originals remain banded, and password XXXL becomes a dense form followed by two strong provider controls.
categories.source_assessment: Contiguous credentials, neutral prompts, fixed pending footprint and measured focus settlement are meaningful improvements. These do not solve overall hierarchy or the placement of auth errors. Preview actions are inert, so authentication success is not evidenced.

categories.name: Settings/account
categories.rationale: Account is orderly and the small prefix change improves guidance scanning.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Identity is passive, sections are native, Home Screen/Lock Screen prefixes are discernible, and lower support/destructive content is reachable. Expanded guidance remains text-heavy at XXXL.
categories.source_assessment: Native insetGrouped List, minimum row heights and attributed prefix emphasis preserve exact text. Refresh/session error paths announce and recover; five Settings methods independently restored recorded originals in supplied evidence.

categories.name: Performance feel
categories.rationale: There is no established runtime responsiveness defect, but hardware feel is not measured.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Movie samples show expected endpoint states and stable focused headings; sparse samples cannot reveal dropped frames or latency.
categories.source_assessment: Current unfiltered suite passes. Five-sample simulator launch/scroll metrics are host/XCTest measurements, not device frame-pacing evidence. Historical notification waits remain unexplained and are not reclassified as an app hang.

categories.name: Delight
categories.rationale: The board has quiet utility; authentication lacks the same effortless finish.
categories.screenshot_assessment: All Clear, the compact composer and subtle Account layout feel considered. Repeated login bars and partially exposed provider controls interrupt that calm.
categories.source_assessment: Semantic feedback and restrained short animations support polish. There is no need for decorative color or extra cards; simplifying existing composition would help most.

categories.name: Long text
categories.rationale: Captured long content is robust and remains readable.
categories.screenshot_assessment: XXXL final board rows retain final lines, instructions wrap, and legal links can be scrolled into view. Activity deliberately tail-truncates per-line previews and reports overflow.
categories.source_assessment: Self-sizing rows, fixedSize vertical helpers, scrollable forms and surface-specific Activity budgets support the observed results. Unbounded real email/provider captions and AX1–AX5 native states remain outside evidence.

categories.name: Reduced Motion / Transparency
categories.rationale: Captured combined settings remain usable and source respects the major preferences.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Combined light/dark default/XXXL error and focus states preserve contrast and headings. The packet records actual native setting restoration, not only launch flags.
categories.source_assessment: Board animation bypasses under Reduce Motion; chrome uses solid alternatives for transparency/contrast. The top mask changes to a short hard boundary. Continuous reduced-motion behavior and Activity on arbitrary backgrounds are not established.

categories.name: Palette / minimalism
categories.rationale: The palette is restrained and mostly semantic.
categories.screenshot_assessment: White/black/gray dominate; indigo identifies credential actions, and red is confined to destructive state. There are no nested custom cards or decorative red/orange surfaces.
categories.source_assessment: System colors and primary/secondary styles avoid palette sprawl. Remaining visual density comes from layout and repeated control surfaces, not a need for more decoration.

findings.screen: Sign In — empty/filled default and password, light/dark, default/XXXL
findings.title: The credential-first composition still has competing horizontal bands
findings.observation: Moving credentials first establishes a useful reading order. The full screen nevertheless reads as field slab, CTA slab, centered mode-switch band, divider, Apple slab, Google outline and legal band. In the dark empty form the native white Apple control dominates the selected email path; at XXXL password size the same ingredients fill the page densely. This is a composition finding, not a failed geometry assertion.
findings.concrete_fix: Keep the native Apple asset, branding, exact words and Apple-then-Google order. Tighten the active field-to-submit cluster to a deliberate 12–16pt rhythm, give the password/link mode switch a quieter leading-aligned typographic treatment with its existing >=44pt hit area, and use one clear spatial break before the provider pair. Reassess whether the divider is still necessary. Review the whole default and password composition together rather than optimizing each gap independently.
findings.regression_check: Recapture the 16 enabled inert composition cases. Retain >=44pt targets, exact copy/provider order, >=4.5:1 active labels, no horizontal clipping and legal-footer reachability; compare the complete screen at native scale for a clear active credential cluster and secondary provider group. Existing 325-test suite must continue passing; taste requires visual acceptance.

findings.screen: Sign In — XXXL empty-password first focus and refocus, normal and combined settings
findings.title: The keyboard Done strip slices through a provider control
findings.observation: Password, its field/helper and the selected action remain visible. The bright Apple button is partially exposed and then abruptly clipped by the opaque Done strip above the keyboard. Other sizes can expose a Google fragment. This makes the focused screen look unfinished despite correct primary focus geometry; it is not evidence that the Password heading is lost.
findings.concrete_fix: Resolve the focused viewport as a composition: attach Done through native keyboard toolbar behavior and tune focused scroll padding/settlement so the provider block is either fully outside the settled viewport or fully visible above Done. Preserve scrolling access to all provider choices, the native asset and the 48pt Done target.
findings.regression_check: Capture first focus, Done dismissal and refocus for empty/filled password at default/XXXL, both appearances and actual combined settings. Measure the settled viewport and provider frames: a provider visible at rest must not be cut across its label or rounded button by the Done surface. Retain existing heading/field/alternate-action bounds and all current focus assertions.

findings.screen: Board — long rows after partial scroll and pull, light/dark XXXL
findings.title: Departing row text leaves a faint custom-looking top fragment
findings.observation: Some departing row lines remain as pale, still-recognizable fragments directly below the title region. The actual Reminders references also soften departing content, so the presence of an edge effect alone is not a defect; Notepad's separate fade and clipped viewport feel less integrated with its navigation chrome. Complete final-row ink remains intact.
findings.concrete_fix: Revisit the custom gradient layer together with the native navigation scroll-edge relationship. Prefer one coordinated native scroll-edge treatment, or an intentional solid boundary under reduced-transparency settings, rather than independent masks. Keep all final-row and composer clearance behavior.
findings.regression_check: Sweep settled partial-scroll offsets through at least 0–100pt in light/dark default/XXXL and combined settings. Inspect the whole first 24pt of the list edge, not only the current 14-pixel test band; record contrast and glyph extents so no isolated crisp fragment sits outside the intended edge treatment. Retain last-row ink, top safe-area and pull-refresh checks.

findings.title: Credential recovery text is separated from the action that needs recovery
source_evidence: ios/App/SignInView.swift: body places error Label after providerSection
findings.observation: The failure message is readable but appears beneath both provider buttons. A user correcting email/password must scan past unrelated alternative actions to find the explanation. This finding concerns placement only; the exact original wording, including Edmund's retained raw network errors elsewhere, stays unchanged.
findings.concrete_fix: Place the existing authentication notice immediately after the active credential action group and before the provider separator, while preserving exact wording, icon and announcement policy. Keep provider-specific errors near the provider action if an existing state distinguishes them.
findings.regression_check: Recapture failure/cleared/reappeared cases in light/dark default/XXXL and combined settings. Require complete notice wrapping and >=4.5:1 text, no duplicate announcements, and credential-action -> notice -> provider ordering for credential errors; retain all existing exact-copy and error-reset checks.

evidence_gaps: No Notes references. The 17 actual Reminders originals provide closest native hierarchy/list/composer/sheet comparisons, not exact auth, Activity, capacity or combined-accessibility-settings counterparts.
Only regular iPhone 17 Pro simulator evidence is established; physical devices, other widths, landscape, Display Zoom and AX1–AX5 are not established.

Protected XCTest keyboard screenshots are partial. Full keyboard judgments use separately labelled actual movie-derived frames; neither source-only frames nor protected stills establish the complete keyboard composition.
All 16 movies were inspected through their three actual sampled frames (48 total) in four supplied inspection sheets. This is not full playback, measured frame pacing or input-latency review.
No physical haptic verification or spoken VoiceOver traversal/rotor session. Those categories rely partly on source and remain provisional.
No true locked-device, Always-On, arbitrary wallpaper, physical Activity lifecycle, live push delivery or exact native Activity reference.

Enabled-looking authentication/Account fixtures are inert previews. No live Apple/Google/password/magic-link authentication, production destructive account action or external-link success is demonstrated.
Five-sample launch/scroll metrics include simulator, host and XCTest overhead. Historical timeout causes are not diagnosed as host load or an app hang.
New filled loading states lack exact Round 7 counterparts; same-state comparison credit is limited to the recorded 60 pairs.
Long real account identities and localization expansion are not covered. Activity single-line truncation is intentional; source caps expanded Island type size at xxxLarge.

categories.name: Visual hierarchy
categories.rationale: Board hierarchy is clear; sign-in still splits attention among several similarly prominent horizontal bands.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Default empty and filled login originals show the email flow first, but the centered alternate method, divider and outlined provider pair compete; dark empty/loading states emphasize Apple most.
categories.source_assessment: SignInView gives major groups uniform 24-point spacing and makes the alternate method full-width. Board uses a clear title/count, rows and pinned composer.

categories.name: Spacing/grid
categories.rationale: Alignment is consistent, but grouping is less intentional on sign-in and expanded Account.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Common left edges are clean. Login fields, action, alternate, divider and providers have a repetitive ladder rhythm; expanded guidance becomes a tall slab.
categories.source_assessment: 20-point form margins and separate 8/20/24-point stacks are predictable. Native Account sections avoid nested cards, though explanatory rows inherit substantial repeated row spacing.

categories.name: Typography scale
categories.rationale: System text is readable and scales coherently, with a little too much equal emphasis in login.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Board body and headers are clear. Notepad branding, Email/Password headings and CTA/link labels compete in XXXL; Home/Lock prefixes improve scanability.
categories.source_assessment: Semantic title2, headline, body and footnote styles are used. Attributed prefix emphasis preserves strings; main alternate authentication action could be visually more subordinate.

categories.name: Dynamic Type
categories.rationale: Default and XXXL are convincingly covered; larger accessibility categories remain unproven.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Long rows, Account instructions and auth helpers wrap without lost final lines in inspected states. Password heading remains visible in full keyboard XXXL captures.
categories.source_assessment: UIKit trait override makes row tests meaningful; fixedSize supports multiline content. Expanded Island explicitly caps at xxxLarge, so this does not establish AX1–AX5 support.

categories.name: Light contrast
categories.rationale: Active text and actions read well; pending feedback is weak.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Primary board and Account text are crisp on white/grouped surfaces. Enabled login preview is distinct from deliberately disabled fixtures; loading spinner is visually faint.
categories.source_assessment: Semantic foreground/background choices and Account explanatory-ink tests support contrast. Disabled appearance should not be mistaken for active-text failure; pending spinner needs separate assessment.

categories.name: Dark contrast
categories.rationale: Strong primary text and neutral surfaces work, but pending-state emphasis is uneven.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Board text remains clear; the white Apple asset dominates empty/loading login while the small spinner recedes into its gray action.
categories.source_assessment: System colors adapt correctly. Native whiteOutline Apple asset is deliberately retained; any hierarchy fix should change surrounding composition, not redraw the Apple asset.

categories.name: Iconography
categories.rationale: Native and restrained symbols communicate roles well.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Completion rings, account symbol, keyboard dismiss, warning and widget symbols are recognizable. No decorative red/orange treatment was seen.
categories.source_assessment: SF Symbols and the native Apple button are preserved. Destructive red is semantic; custom six-dot reorder grip is modest, with a larger interaction target.

categories.name: Safe area / Dynamic Island
categories.rationale: Main controls and Activity content respect the measured device geometry.
categories.screenshot_assessment: No title/account collision with the Island; final board rows clear the footer. Expanded Activity text remains inside the black system shape.
categories.source_assessment: Safe-area insets, native navigation and explicit Activity layout margins support observed results. Only the regular iPhone 17 Pro geometry is established.

categories.name: Scroll/pull-down / last row
categories.rationale: Last-row legibility and refresh settlement are strong; top-edge fade is slightly untidy.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Both themes and sizes retain the final row above the capacity footer after pull/scroll. Some preceding-row glyphs remain faintly visible at the upper edge.
categories.source_assessment: Native UICollectionView refresh and measured final-ink tests address real risks. Custom 24-point gradient top mask explains the residual fade, rather than a missing bottom inset.

categories.name: List rows
categories.rationale: Rows are readable, spacious and mechanically coherent.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Long paragraphs retain alignment, separation and full text; completion rings align to first lines. Persistent grips add a little visual noise compared with Reminders.
categories.source_assessment: UIHostingConfiguration in native list cells, multiline body text and explicit completion/reorder accessibility actions are sound. Drag behavior is source/test-supported, not hands-on reviewed.

categories.name: Empty states
categories.rationale: The next action is clear, but setup instructions dominate the otherwise calm empty board.
categories.screenshot_assessment: All Clear plus bottom composer is legible. The long three-step setup tip occupies more visual attention than the empty-state invitation, especially XXXL.
categories.source_assessment: ContentUnavailableView and dismissible persisted setup guidance are native-minded. Guidance is hidden during composition, which protects the active task.

categories.name: Composer ergonomics
categories.rationale: Composer is accessible and well separated from the list.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Typed multiline draft, dismiss key and add action remain visible above the keyboard; capacity state is clearly noneditable.
categories.source_assessment: SafeAreaInset, 1–4-line input, 44-point targets and capacity replacement are appropriate. The tests exercise edge taps and final-row geometry.

categories.name: Keyboard handling
categories.rationale: Focus settlement works, while the provider/Done boundary is visually awkward.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Actual first-focus and refocus XXXL frames preserve Password heading, field and alternate action. The opaque Done strip cuts off the lower Apple button border; email variants can expose part of Google.
categories.source_assessment: Measured focus frames, idle settlement and keyboardDidShow handling are more robust than guessed offsets. Safe-area Done inset creates a hard visual cutoff below the primary work area.

categories.name: Sheet presentation/detents
categories.rationale: Account uses a coherent native sheet with appropriate expansion.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Medium and large detents, grabber, pinned Done and scrolled content are convincing. Long guidance scrolls rather than squeezing.
categories.source_assessment: Native presentationDetents, scroll interaction and insetGrouped List are appropriate. Expanded long guidance still requires substantial traversal at medium size.

categories.name: Navigation clarity
categories.rationale: The limited navigation is understandable.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Board account affordance, Account Done, method-switch actions and inbox confirmation are explicit. Providers remain Apple then Google.
categories.source_assessment: NavigationStack, explicit dismissal and method state changes preserve a simple structure. External and authenticated navigation is not established by inert fixtures.

categories.name: Touch targets
categories.rationale: Measured targets and visible spacing are strong within tested states.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Completion, add, Done, clear and main login actions have generous apparent targets. Full keyboard captures do not show focused field/action collision.
categories.source_assessment: 44-point minimums, 48-point sign-in Done and provider height, native rows and edge-tap UI tests support the score. No claim of arbitrary-device or motor-accessibility testing.

categories.name: Haptics
categories.rationale: Intent is sensible, but physical feel cannot be established from this packet.
categories.screenshot_assessment: No still image or sampled video can establish tactile strength, timing or duplication.
categories.source_assessment: Success/error sensory feedback and drag selection feedback are present. Physical-device confirmation of add/complete/reorder/auth feedback remains absent; score is provisional.

categories.name: Animation/transitions
categories.rationale: Sampled transitions show no gross layout failure, but motion quality is only partially evidenced.
categories.screenshot_assessment: All 16 movies were represented by three actual sampled frames each. Focus and Activity state changes look coherent in those samples; full playback/frame pacing was not reviewed.
categories.source_assessment: Reduced-motion branches and native presentation are sensible. The historical XCTest timeout is not evidence of an app animation hang, nor do passed tests establish smoothness.

categories.name: Loading states
categories.rationale: Fixed action geometry is an improvement; busy feedback needs more visual presence.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Filled/loading/baseline triplets retain neighboring positions. Small muted spinner within a large disabled-looking action is less evident than the nearby Apple asset.
categories.source_assessment: Invisible retained title plus overlay spinner preserves layout and accessible progress wording. Geometry/spinner-pixel tests verify stability and existence, not perceived prominence.

categories.name: Error states
categories.rationale: Errors are visible, recoverable and avoid destructive-looking decoration.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Board empty/populated errors, retry/dismiss, Account refresh failure and sign-in error are legible in both themes and combined settings.
categories.source_assessment: Announcements are deduplicated without forced focus movement. Raw board network-error wording is explicitly retained by user instruction and is not a finding.

categories.name: VoiceOver/labels
categories.rationale: Source and label tests are thoughtful, but spoken traversal remains unobserved.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Raster evidence cannot prove reading order, announcements or rotor usability.
categories.source_assessment: Unique Password field label, hidden duplicate heading, progress labels, completion/reorder actions and deduplicated error announcements are appropriate. Spoken VoiceOver sessions remain a gap.

categories.name: iOS HIG consistency
categories.rationale: Native components give a strong foundation; login composition feels more assembled than polished.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Account and board resemble native list/sheet idioms. Login combines native Apple, custom Google border, rounded input/action and independent centered link into a busier composition.
categories.source_assessment: NavigationStack, ContentUnavailableView, native collection list and Apple authorization button are appropriate. Custom masks and keyboard inset deserve careful visual review.

categories.name: Lock Screen / Live Activity
categories.rationale: Captured banner and expanded Island states are readable within a deliberately limited line budget.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Long text tails truncate and +more counts are clear. Sampled expansion/banner changes do not show collisions; the wallpaper is only one tested background.
categories.source_assessment: Explicit line budgeting and hidden-count handling are coherent, with xxxLarge cap on Island. True locked-device, Always-On, alternate wallpaper and exact Apple Activity references are absent.

categories.name: Sign-in/onboarding
categories.rationale: Email-first is a real improvement, but the screen still feels crowded and lacks a clear secondary hierarchy.
categories.screenshot_assessment: All 60 same-state pairs were inspected. Empty and filled default originals retain too many competing bands; XXXL password pushes providers/legal into scrolling. The latter is reachable, not a lost-content claim.
categories.source_assessment: Contiguous email/password work area, preserved provider order, isolated fixtures and fixed pending footprint are good. Uniform group spacing and a prominent alternate method leave the central composition unresolved.

categories.name: Settings/account
categories.rationale: Native grouping and stronger prefixes help, while expanded explanations remain dense.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Statuses and actions are clear; Home Screen/Lock Screen prefix weight is visible. Expanded instruction rows plus permanent multi-paragraph footer fill much of the sheet.
categories.source_assessment: BoardPersistenceSection changes preserve words and improve prefix hierarchy. DisclosureGroup and insetGrouped List are appropriate; footnote text still needs better subdivision without deleting copy.

categories.name: Performance feel
categories.rationale: Available evidence supports functioning transitions, not hardware-level responsiveness.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Sampled films and settled screenshots show no gross stall; they cannot establish input latency or frame consistency.
categories.source_assessment: Five-sample public launch/scroll metrics are simulator/host/XCTest evidence. Full-suite passes and binary binding support reproducibility; no physical profiling or arbitrary slowdown diagnosis is claimed.

categories.name: Delight
categories.rationale: The app is calm and direct, but polished composition is uneven.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Readable board and quiet palette are pleasing. Login's repetitive boxes and expanded Account's instruction mass reduce the feeling of a finished native tool.
categories.source_assessment: Simple interactions and restrained feedback create a good base. The remaining opportunity is spacing, emphasis and transitions, not decorative color, new branding or extra cards.

categories.name: Long text
categories.rationale: Long-content treatment is strong in the tested board and Account states.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Full final paragraphs are visible after traversal at XXXL; helpers wrap. Activity truncation is intentional and accompanied by hidden-line counts.
categories.source_assessment: Unbounded row text, fixed vertical sizing and independent ideal-height/ink checks support the board. Long real account identities and localized strings are not demonstrated.

categories.name: Reduced Motion / Transparency
categories.rationale: Actual combined settings provide stronger evidence than environment overrides alone.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Combined-setting login and Account/error captures remain readable and stable, including full first-focus/refocus witnesses.
categories.source_assessment: All five methods independently restored four original switches 0/1/0/0. Reduced-motion branches and solid edge-mask fallback exist; full subjective motion comfort is unobserved.

categories.name: Palette / minimalism
categories.rationale: Restrained colors and absence of nested cards fit the requested direction.
categories.screenshot_assessment: Neutral board and Account surfaces, sparse functional purple and semantic destructive red are consistent. Login's visual density comes from structure rather than decorative colors.
categories.source_assessment: System colors and native asset preservation are appropriate. Continue reducing competing framing/spacing, without changing words, branding, icons or adding red/orange decoration.

findings.screen: Sign In: default empty/filled and XXXL password
findings.title: Email-first ordering has improved the flow, but the composition still has too many competing bands
findings.observation: The page repeats broad field, broad action, centered full-width alternate method, a divider with generous surrounding gaps, two outlined provider controls and a separate legal row. The email action becomes clear when filled, but empty/pending states let the native Apple asset become the strongest object. This is composition and hierarchy, not a request to modify Apple's asset or hide required words.
findings.concrete_fix: Keep the contiguous email-first flow. Make the existing alternate-method text a leading-aligned callout within that flow, retaining a minimum 44-point target. Replace uniform large inter-group gaps with explicit field/action and section gaps; start by reducing spacing around the divider from 24 to 16 points while keeping the Apple/Google pair together at its existing order and native Apple styling. Keep legal links in a quieter, reachable footer. Compare complete default empty and filled screens before accepting the change; do not add cards.
findings.regression_check: Recapture the same 60 paired states, especially both default empty/filled themes and XXXL password. Assert every original string and native Apple asset/order remain, targets stay >=44 points, default field/CTA/alternate/provider/footer bounds do not overlap, and XXXL legal links remain reachable by a real gesture. Run the existing iOS suite; visual side-by-side review must separately accept the new hierarchy.

findings.screen: Sign In: settled empty-password keyboard, first focus/refocus
findings.title: The opaque Done strip cuts through a provider control at the settled keyboard boundary
findings.confidence: high for appearance; medium for proposed layout adjustment
findings.observation: Actual full-screen first-focus/refocus XXXL witnesses keep Password, input, helper and alternate method clear, which is a successful fix. Below that work area, the Apple button's lower border is cut off by the Done strip; some email captures expose only part of Google. This is a small polish defect at automatic settlement, not proof that the provider is unreachable and not a protected-screenshot artifact.
findings.concrete_fix: Make the automatic focus settlement respect the boundary after the primary form group as well as the focused heading. When a provider cannot fit wholly above Done, add focused-state separation so that the initial resting viewport ends in the gap before the provider group; keep the complete group in the same scroll view and reachable by user scrolling or keyboard dismissal. Do not shrink the native Apple control or force all controls into the keyboard viewport.
findings.regression_check: Use actual unmodified full-screen frames for first focus and refocus, light/dark, default/XXXL, normal/combined settings. Require full heading, field, helper and primary/alternate actions inside the viewport, >=44-point targets, and no provider label or border intersecting the Done strip at automatic settled positions. Exercise manual scroll and Done so providers/legal remain reachable; preserve existing focus/geometry assertions and run the iOS suite.

findings.title: Stable pending geometry leaves an overly faint busy indicator
findings.observation: The new overlay retains the button footprint, but the small muted spinner recedes into a large gray disabled-looking surface while the nearby Apple asset stays visually forceful. The current tests show stable geometry and spinner pixels, not readable progress prominence. No numerical contrast failure is asserted here.
findings.concrete_fix: Keep the invisible retained title and fixed footprint, but style the progress indicator explicitly with a stronger semantic foreground that remains visible under the disabled button environment. Keep the existing accessible in-progress wording and do not enlarge surrounding chrome or change copy.
findings.regression_check: Retain baseline/loading/baseline y/width/height tolerance checks for both methods, sizes and themes. Add a raster check that the spinner's strongest visible strokes reach at least 3:1 against the measured button fill in both themes, and inspect the whole screen to confirm pending work is apparent. Run the existing iOS suite.

findings.screen: Account: expanded Add a lasting widget guidance
findings.title: Prefix emphasis helps, but the expanded guidance remains visually dense
findings.observation: Home Screen and Lock Screen prefixes now scan better. The two long instruction rows, widget caveat and permanent multi-paragraph footer still read as a continuous instructional block and push the next task far below the fold, especially at XXXL/medium detent. This is density, not clipping or insufficient measured text contrast.
findings.concrete_fix: Preserve every string but place each emphasized Home Screen:/Lock Screen: prefix on its own line above its instruction body, with a small internal gap and consistent inter-instruction spacing. Keep the widget caveat visibly subordinate within the disclosure and separate the permanent footer from subsequent action sections using the existing native section structure. Avoid additional card backgrounds.
findings.regression_check: Recapture expanded/collapsed Account at both detents, themes and sizes. Require exact original concatenated strings, >=7:1 explanatory-text contrast, first/final-line ink, and existing >=16-point inter-section boundary checks. Verify both instruction prefixes are visually distinct without reducing body size, and all lower actions remain reachable. Run the iOS suite.

findings.screen: Board: partially scrolled long/full rows, normal and populated error
findings.title: Faint preceding-row fragments make the custom upper fade slightly untidy
findings.observation: Faded text fragments remain directly below the navigation/error boundary after settling. Native Reminders also uses scroll-edge translucency, so this is a modest integration difference, not a general ban on partially visible rows or a safe-area failure. The final row and footer are clear.
findings.concrete_fix: Tune the existing custom top mask so its fully transparent strip aligns with the actual native scroll-edge boundary before the transition begins, rather than fading half a glyph immediately beneath a hard boundary. Compare with the matched Reminders top/bottom references; preserve pull refresh, native edge behavior and the solid fallback for accessibility settings.
findings.regression_check: Repeat real pull then 83/47/61-point partial drags in both themes/sizes and populated-error states. Extend the existing upper-band raster witness to inspect the mask transition boundary and confirm no isolated crisp glyph fragments appear at the boundary, while the next complete line remains readable. Re-run final-row ink/geometry, refresh settlement and the iOS suite; judge the fade against native references separately.
